newsitem.title: USA: Ford, UAW say they reached tentative labor agreement.
newsitem.headline: Ford, UAW say they reached tentative labor agreement.

text.p: Ford Motor Co. and the United Auto Workers union said Monday they had reached a tentative agreement on a new national labor pact.
Ford and UAW officials, at a news conference here, declined to provide details of the pact but said they expected it to be ratified by Sept. 29.
UAW President Stephen Yokich said the agreement will be presented to the union's Ford council on Wednesday.

The pact, which covers Ford's 105,000 UAW hourly workers, was reached after marathon bargaining sessions over the weekend and Monday. Ford's previous three-year contract with the UAW expired at midnight on Saturday.
UAW officials declined to comment on the length of the current pact, but Ford Chairman Alex Trotman said earlier Monday that the two sides had discussed several term lengths beyond three years.

Yokich said he had not decided yet whether to target General Motors Corp. or Chrysler Corp. for the next round of bargaining. He said the decision would be based partly on the outcome of the Canadian talks with Chrysler.
